title: Faithful servants (Matthew 24:32–51)
hookLine: a soft new leaf, an hour nobody knows, and a servant found doing his job
tomorrow: ten young women, a late groom, and five lamps going out…

cards: Run a thumb along a brand-new leaf in spring. Soft, thin, almost damp, nothing like the tough leaves at the end of summer. Jesus asks his friends to learn from exactly that.
"Now learn a parable of the fig tree; When his branch is yet tender, and putteth forth leaves, ye know that summer is nigh." You can feel a season coming.
But the day and hour of the end, he says, nobody knows, "no, not the angels of heaven, but my Father only." So if no one knows when, what are you meant to be doing?

teach.b: He answers with ordinary pictures. Noah's neighbors, eating and drinking and marrying, right up to the day of the flood. A householder who would have stayed awake if he'd known when the thief was coming.

"Who then is a faithful and wise servant, whom his lord hath made ruler over his household, to give them meat in due season?" Meat here means the household's meals. His job is plain: feed everyone, on time.
"Blessed is that servant, whom his lord when he cometh shall find so doing." So doing. Not staring at the sky.
Not working out the date. Hands busy with the work in front of him. Then the other servant, who "shall say in his heart, My lord delayeth his coming."
He starts beating his fellow servants and drinking with the drunken. His failure isn't a wrong guess about the hour.

It's that the delay became an excuse. And notice where the parable is set: not a battlefield or a mountaintop, but a house at mealtime, with people waiting to be fed. Readiness in this chapter doesn't mean knowing when.
It means being found at your post, with the bread on the table, whenever the door opens.

how: Christians read this parable alongside the line that no one knows the day or hour, and hear it as a call to faithful daily work rather than to date-setting.

games.q: a guy online posts a chart claiming he's worked out the exact year of the end from the signs. by Matthew 24:36, what's the reply?
o: no one knows the day or hour, not even the angels.
maybe: if the signs line up, the date can be decoded.
fine, as long as he's sure enough to post it.
games.why: Jesus says of that day and hour knoweth no man, no, not the angels of heaven, but my Father only. then he points to the servant found doing his job.

practice: Pick up the tool of one ordinary job waiting for you today: a pen, a sponge, your keys, a spatula, a phone. Hold it in both hands, and feel its weight, its edges, whether it is warm or cool.
Let it stand for the work in front of you, the household's bread in due season, and breathe with it in your hands. When the sit ends, set it down where you will see it.

wordCard.voice: Faithful servants. In Jesus' parable, the ones found doing their daily work, feeding the household, when the master comes home.

orig.note: Greek for faithful, in Matthew 24:45: a faithful and wise servant.

carryVoice: Pocket this one: found doing it, the blessing that lands on ordinary work. Talk soon.
